_meta.indication: TRYPTYR is indicated for the treatment of the signs and symptoms of dry eye disease.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, multi-center, double-masked, vehicle (placebo)-controlled study; dosed twice a day for 90 days
pivotal_trials.population: Subjects 30 years of age and older with signs and symptoms of dry eye disease
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of subjects with a >=10-mm increase (postdrop on Day 14 versus predrop at baseline) in unanesthetized Schirmer score on Day 14
pivotal_trials.result: 42.6% of TRYPTYR patients achieved >=10 mm increase in Schirmer score at Day 14 vs 8.2% of vehicle (difference 34.4%, 95% CI 26.9, 42.0; p<0.01)

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, multi-center, double-masked, vehicle (placebo)-controlled study; dosed twice a day for 90 days
pivotal_trials.population: Subjects 30 years of age and older with signs and symptoms of dry eye disease
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of subjects with a >=10-mm increase (postdrop on Day 14 versus predrop at baseline) in unanesthetized Schirmer score on Day 14
pivotal_trials.result: 53.2% of TRYPTYR patients achieved >=10 mm increase in Schirmer score at Day 14 vs 14.4% of vehicle (difference 38.8%, 95% CI 30.8, 46.8; p<0.01)

key_safety: Most common adverse reaction was instillation site pain (50%). Less than 1% of patients discontinued therapy due to burning or stinging sensation in the eyes.
target_moa: Acoltremon is an agonist of transient receptor potential melastatin 8 (TRPM8) thermoreceptors; TRPM8 stimulation activates trigeminal nerve signaling leading to increased basal tear production.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was held for this application.

summary.text: NDA 217370 was reviewed by a multidisciplinary team as a Standard Review and was not presented at an advisory committee.
